title: Artificial Intelligence for the evaluation of esophageal strictures
summary:
In patients with a narrowing of the esophagus (food pipe), accurately determining the diameter of the narrowed area is important for planning further treatment. Currently, this assessment is usually based on the subjective visual judgment of the physician performing an endoscopic examination of the esophagus and stomach.
The aim of this study is to investigate how much the assessments of different physicians vary when estimating the diameter of an esophageal narrowing. To do this, several reviewers will independently evaluate the same endoscopic video recordings and estimate the diameter of the narrowed segment.
In addition, an artificial intelligence (AI)-based method will be developed to automatically measure the diameter of the narrowing. The results obtained by the AI system will be compared with the assessments made by the physicians and evaluated for their accuracy.
In the long term, this approach may help to provide a more objective, standardized, and reproducible assessment of esophageal narrowings, thereby supporting clinical decision-making and patient care.

interventions.name: Participant recruitment is anticipated to take place between July 2026 and July 2027. Patients with esophageal strictures and an independently established clinical indication for endoscopic dilation using either balloon or bougie techniques will be eligible for inclusion. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Independent clinical indication for diagnostic and/or interventional gastrointestinal endoscopy for esophageal stricture
2. Patients capable of giving consent and aged > 18 years
3. Sufficient proficiency in the German language, both verbally and in writing
4. Written informed consent for study participation available
Exclusion criteria:
1. Contraindication to the planned endoscopic procedure
2. ASA-classification > 3
